questions.stem: Which factor increases the rate of transpiration?
questions.explanation: Increased wind speed moves humid air away from the leaf surface, maintaining a steep water potential gradient between the inside of the leaf and the outside air, increasing transpiration.

questions.stem: Why does high humidity decrease the rate of transpiration?

options.text: It reduces the water potential gradient between the leaf and the air, so less water vapour diffuses out

questions.explanation: High humidity means the air already contains a lot of water vapour, reducing the concentration gradient for water between the inside of the leaf and the outside air, slowing diffusion.

questions.stem: How does increased light intensity affect transpiration?

options.text: It increases transpiration because stomata open wider for gas exchange during photosynthesis

questions.explanation: In bright light, stomata open wider to allow carbon dioxide in for photosynthesis. With stomata open wider, more water vapour can escape, increasing the rate of transpiration.

questions.stem: Why does increasing temperature increase the rate of transpiration?

options.text: Water molecules have more kinetic energy and evaporate faster from mesophyll cell surfaces

questions.explanation: Higher temperatures give water molecules more kinetic energy, increasing the rate of evaporation from the surfaces of mesophyll cells inside the leaf, and thus increasing transpiration.

questions.stem: What is the role of guard cells in controlling transpiration?

options.text: They open and close stomata, regulating water loss

questions.explanation: Guard cells control the opening and closing of stomata. When turgid, they open the stoma allowing gas exchange; when flaccid, they close it to reduce water loss.

questions.stem: A plant in still, humid, cool, dark conditions would have:

options.text: The same rate as in windy, dry, hot conditions
A very low rate of transpiration
A very high rate of transpiration

questions.explanation: Still, humid, cool, dark conditions minimise transpiration: stomata tend to close in the dark, cool temperatures reduce evaporation, high humidity reduces the gradient, and no wind means no removal of vapour.

questions.stem: How can a plant reduce water loss on a hot day?
questions.explanation: Plants can close their stomata to reduce water loss through transpiration on hot days. However, this also limits CO2 intake for photosynthesis, so it is a trade-off.
